items.title: Aging
items.moral: Moral: Growing older brings more than a loss of strength. Experience and wisdom can also give us a broader view of life.
body: Aging is like climbing a mountain: the higher you rise, the more tired you become and the shorter your breath, yet the wider your view of the world grows.

items.title: Eyes That Do Not See
items.moral: Moral: True sight requires understanding as well as eyes. We can look without seeing and listen without understanding.
body: The world is full of blind people who think they see because they have eyes.

items.moral: Moral: Older people offer the wisdom of experience, while children remind us of innocence. Every stage of life has something to teach us.

items.title: The One Left Behind
items.moral: Moral: The person left behind carries both love and longing. Separation can make the depth of that love painfully clear.
body: When two people love each other wholeheartedly and one dies, the survivor may feel that they, too, have ceased to live.

items.title: Be Mindful of What You Say
items.moral: Moral: Be careful not to deepen another person’s sense of loss. They need understanding, not reminders of what they lack.
body: Do not dwell on your wealth in front of someone who is poor, your health in front of someone who is ill, or your happiness in front of someone who is suffering. Be equally thoughtful when speaking of freedom to a prisoner, strength to someone who is weak, children to someone who has none, or parents to an orphan.

items.title: Do You Have Enough Money?
items.moral: Moral: Show your parents that you value them through practical care. No one and nothing can replace them.
body: Value your parents while they are alive. Instead of merely asking, “Do you have enough money?” do what you can to meet their needs. No one can take their place.

items.title: Speak Kindly or Remain Silent
items.moral: Moral: Words have value when we use them thoughtfully and for good. If you have nothing worthwhile to say, silence may be the wiser choice.
body: If you're not going to open your mouth to say something nice, don't open it at all.
